content.reading:
OFFICIAL ALIGNMENT
REB Senior 1 Mathematics, Unit 1: Sets.

SUPERTEACHER DEEP EXPLANATION
A set is a membership rule, not merely a list. A useful rule gives a definite yes-or-no result for every candidate. “Students in Senior 1” is well-defined; “very clever students” is not until cleverness has a stated measure.

Statement, roster and set-builder forms are three representations of the same rule. Translating between them tests whether you understand the property behind the symbols.
content.deep_explanation:
LAYER 1 — MEMBERSHIP
For A = {multiples of 3 below 15}, 12 ∈ A but 14 ∉ A.

LAYER 2 — REPRESENTATION
{2,4,6,8} = {positive even integers below 10} = {x ∈ N | x is even and x < 10}.

LAYER 3 — CONTAINMENT
A ⊆ B means every member of A is also a member of B. One counterexample is enough to disprove a proposed subset relationship.

COMMON TRAP
Order and repetition do not change a set. {1,2,2,3} and {3,2,1} are the same set.
content.examples:
Example 1
Write the first five positive multiples of 4 in roster form.
Solution: {4, 8, 12, 16, 20}.

Example 2
Let A be the positive multiples of 6 and B the positive even numbers. Is A ⊆ B?
Solution: Yes. Every multiple of 6 is divisible by 2.
content.practice:
1. Which is well-defined: beautiful songs, prime numbers below 30, or tall students?
2. Write {5,10,15,20} in set-builder form.
3. List every subset of {a,b}.
4. Prove that multiples of 10 form a subset of multiples of 5.
5. Give one counterexample showing that integers are not a subset of natural numbers.
content.practice_answers:
1. Prime numbers below 30.
2. {x ∈ N | x is a multiple of 5 and 5 ≤ x ≤ 20}.
3. ∅, {a}, {b}, {a,b}.
4. 10k = 5(2k), so every multiple of 10 is a multiple of 5.
5. −1 is an integer but not a natural number.
content.summary: A set needs an objective membership rule. Equivalent representations preserve the same rule. A subset claim must hold for every member.

quiz.question: Which description is a well-defined set?

content.experiment: Classify twenty classroom objects using two different objective rules. Record which objects change groups when the rule changes.
content.assignment: Design a decision tree that tells a younger learner whether an object belongs to a set. Include three valid and two invalid membership rules.
